selected_evidence.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 ICMP redirect and source-route acceptance
selected_evidence.summary: Shows the installed persistent file, all effective values at 0, and the same values remaining 0 after reboot.

Captures healthy baseline boot ID d878c725-2044-4902-af67-a254c5d0a6c2, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID c8f3f9e4-e222-4624-8846-fd8a215bd052, and recovered sysctl/networking/chronyd/vsock-agent/sshd services with address, route, and reachability intact.

Kernel system variables configuration files

Files found under the /etc/sysctl.d directory that end with .conf are
parsed within sysctl(8) at boot time.  If you want to set kernel variables
you can either edit /etc/sysctl.conf or make a new file.

The filename isn't important, but don't make it a package name as it may clash
with something the package builder needs later. The file name must end
with .conf, or it will not be read.

The recommended location for local system settings is /etc/sysctl.d/local.conf
but as long as you follow the rules for the name of the file, anything will
work. see the sysctl.conf(5) man page for details of the format. This manpage
can be found in the `procps-doc` package.

commands.command:
set -eu
umask 022
cat > /tmp/99-network-hardening.conf <<'ANTRIEB_EOF'
# Disable IPv4 ICMP redirect and source-route acceptance.
# "default" protects interfaces created later; explicit current interfaces
# ensure the running and boot-time interface instances are hardened too.
net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects = 0
net.ipv4.conf.default.accept_redirects = 0
net.ipv4.conf.eth0.accept_redirects = 0
net.ipv4.conf.lo.accept_redirects = 0
net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route = 0
net.ipv4.conf.default.accept_source_route = 0
net.ipv4.conf.eth0.accept_source_route = 0
net.ipv4.conf.lo.accept_source_route = 0
ANTRIEB_EOF
install -o root -g root -m 0644 /tmp/99-network-hardening.conf /etc/sysctl.d/99-network-hardening.conf
rm /tmp/99-network-hardening.conf
sysctl -p /etc/sysctl.d/99-network-hardening.conf
printf 'persisted_file:\n'; cat /etc/sysctl.d/99-network-hardening.conf
printf 'file_metadata:\n'; stat -c '%U:%G %a %n' /etc/sysctl.d/99-network-hardening.conf

commands.command:
set -eu
printf 'pre_reboot_boot_id='; cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
nohup sh -c 'sleep 2; /sbin/reboot' >/tmp/antrieb-reboot.log 2>&1 &
printf 'reboot_scheduled=acknowledged\n'

set -eu
old_boot_id='d878c725-2044-4902-af67-a254c5d0a6c2'
new_boot_id=$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id)
printf 'old_boot_id=%s\nnew_boot_id=%s\n' "$old_boot_id" "$new_boot_id"
[ "$new_boot_id" != "$old_boot_id" ] && printf 'boot_identity_changed=yes\n'
printf 'effective_values_after_reboot:\n'; for f in /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/*/accept_redirects /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/*/accept_source_route; do printf '%s=' "$f"; cat "$f"; test "$(cat "$f")" = 0; done
printf 'persistent_file_after_reboot:\n'; cat /etc/sysctl.d/99-network-hardening.conf
printf 'required_services_after_reboot:\n'; for s in sysctl networking chronyd vsock-agent sshd; do printf '%s: ' "$s"; rc-service "$s" status; done
printf 'ipv4_address_after_reboot='; ip -4 -o addr show dev eth0 | awk '{print $4}'
printf 'default_route_after_reboot='; ip -4 route show default
printf 'self_reachability_after_reboot='; ping -c 1 -W 2 "$NODE_IP" >/dev/null && printf 'ok\n'
